dedupe_keys.name: ixp us connected nation internet exchange points target locations for regional us exchanges

description: IXP.US, trading name of Connected Nation Internet Exchange Points, is building carrier-neutral internet exchange points in regional hub cities of the United States that lack neutral interconnection or a peering fabric, and publishes the list of places it plans to serve. Its one-page target list names 135 communities in 47 states and four US territories, from Anchorage and Fairbanks in Alaska to Pago Pago in American Samoa, Saipan, St. Croix and three sites in Puerto Rico, many of them university towns. The first, or alpha, site is at Wichita State University in Kansas, and the website reports more than 260 peers on the DE-CIX exchange fabric reached through its facilities and ten university partnerships so far. The venture is a 50/50 partnership between the non-profit Connected Nation and Newby Ventures, led by the carrier-hotel developer Hunter Newby, and pitches the sites as a way to lower latency for AI and cloud services and cut wholesale transit costs. Coverage: planned sites across the United States. Format and access: website and a PDF list of target cities, free. Caveats: a plan from the developer, not a record of built sites; the list changes as sites open, and the document link is a hosted file, not a stable dataset. Simulation uses: scenarios of future interconnection hubs in underserved regions, shorter paths and more route diversity in network models, and planning of regional resilience. Related records: the World Bank and CAIDA exchange lists hold existing exchanges.
